claim.text: Transit shape and host-star parameters can separate astrophysical false positives from genuine planets without using the light curve.

final_verdict.statement: **Stage 6 verdict: supported** on the adjudicated sample: **0.838 ± 0.005** balanced accuracy (random forest, 5-fold CV grouped by host star) against a computed majority floor of **0.500** and a 12-repeat permuted-label null of **0.531 ± 0.010**. The claim is supported for adjudicated TOIs only; extending it to the open candidates would require a selection-effect correction this run does not attempt.

concepts: curved-boundary test as a degree sweep · a tree you can read aloud · memorisation onset from the depth curve
narrative: **Logistic.** Degree 1 scores **0.734** balanced accuracy (AUC **0.792**) on the held-out hosts; adding degree-2 terms lifts it to **0.802** (AUC **0.865**) — the boundary is measurably curved, as in the reference run. The largest standardised coefficients are `log10_pl_trandep log10_pl_rade` (+2.42) and `log10_pl_rade^2` (-2.19); positive pushes toward 'planet'.

**CART.** Held-out accuracy peaks around depth **7** and the train-test gap at the shipped depth 5 is **0.065** — deeper trees memorise. The shipped tree scores **0.757** balanced accuracy (AUC **0.802**); the exported depth-3 tree opens on `log10_pl_insol`, the same radius-first logic the reference tree found. Both models clearly beat the floor; the CV stage gives the adjudicated numbers.

concepts: ranking vs decisions vs probabilities — three separate claims · would more data help
narrative: **Ranking.** The ensembles lead: AUC **0.900** (RF) and **0.900** (GB) against **0.865** for the degree-2 logistic and **0.802** for the depth-5 tree, all on the identical 811-row held-out side (404 planets, 407 false positives).

**Decisions.** At the default threshold the RF catches **0.76** of false positives and **0.91** of planets — the 0.24 of false positives that survive would waste follow-up time, the 0.09 of planets lost would drop real targets from the queue; which error costs more is a telescope-time judgment, not a statistics one.

**Probabilities.** RF votes track observed frequencies well: ECE **0.053**, Brier **0.126**, with 2 bin(s) beyond binomial noise. **More data?** The grouped learning curve rises to **0.838** at the full ~2,154-row training size with a last-step gain of **+0.007** against a fold spread of 0.010 — plateaued: collecting more rows alike to these buys little; features, not rows.

stages.title: Adjudication: grouped cross-validation with its floors
stages.summary: Host-grouped 5-fold CV: random forest 0.838 ± 0.005 balanced accuracy vs CART 0.753 and logistic 0.811, against a computed majority floor of 0.500 and a 12-repeat permuted-label null of 0.531 ± 0.010 — the signal is real and host-grouping-proof.

provenance.method: 5-fold GroupKFold by tid over the full adjudicated set; per fold the entire pipeline (median impute + z-score (+ expansion) + model) refit from scratch on the other folds; balanced accuracy headline, ROC AUC alongside; majority floor computed under the same folds. Pipelines received as in-kernel objects from stages 3-4 and cloned per fold (D11)

inputs.preprocessing: full adjudicated set, post-log unscaled matrix; all fitted state inside the per-fold pipelines

provenance.method: 12-repeat permuted-label null of the best pipeline (random forest): labels exchanged between equal-size host groups (block permutation), full pipeline re-run under the identical fold scheme per repeat

inputs.preprocessing: identical folds and pipeline as the host CV

concepts: the fold is the independent unit · floors computed under the same folds · a permutation null floors the whole pipeline
narrative: Under host-grouped 5-fold cross-validation the random forest scores **0.838 ± 0.005** balanced accuracy (AUC **0.910**), the depth-5 CART **0.753 ± 0.004**, and the degree-2 logistic **0.811 ± 0.008** — the same ordering as the reference snapshot (0.826 / 0.750 / 0.703 there), on a nearly balanced sample where the majority floor is **0.500**, not the reference's 0.539.

The permuted-label null — the whole random forest pipeline re-run 12 times with labels exchanged between equal-size host blocks under the identical folds — lands at **0.531 ± 0.010**. The observed mean sits **30** null standard deviations above it: the score is not an artefact of pipeline flexibility, class balance, or host-block structure. The null mean sits above 0.500 — expected under block permutation, which preserves each host's label vector: multi-TOI hosts are planet-rich and recognisable from their stellar columns, and that association survives the shuffle. This makes it a stricter, more honest floor than naive row-wise label shuffling (the reference run's 0.500).
No host star spans a fold boundary, so no stellar column is shared between a training and a scoring fold; these are the adjudicated numbers the header verdict rests on.

GroupKFold folds are deterministic (size-balanced), so fold class balance is not stratified; the fold-dispersion sanity check reports the spread.
The permuted null was run for the best pipeline only (12 x 5 forest refits); nulls for the other pipelines would cost the same again and were not part of the plan.
gradient_boosting was not CV-scored (plan mirrors the reference's three-pipeline adjudication); its single-split numbers live in stages 4-5.

stages.title: Leak probe: pl_eqt restored
stages.summary: Restoring pl_eqt to the otherwise-identical logistic CV pipeline moves balanced accuracy 0.811 -> 0.815 (delta +0.004 vs fold se 0.008): no illicit signal detected by this probe; the headline scores remain the ones without the column.

provenance.method: pl_eqt fetched from the raw table, log10-transformed like its sibling physical columns, appended to the feature matrix, and passed through the IDENTICAL logistic degree-2 grouped-CV pipeline and folds as the stage-6 reference score; the feature list is the only change

inputs.preprocessing: in-pipeline median impute + z-score + degree-2 expansion, refit per fold

concepts: price the leak in report units · one change only · the honest score is the one without the column
narrative: pl_eqt was excluded from every feature matrix in both smoke runs because it is derivable from pl_insol and, in the reference run, its computation convention tracked the label. Restored to the otherwise-identical logistic CV pipeline it moves the score from **0.811** to **0.815** — a delta of **+0.004** against a fold standard error of **0.008**. The delta sits within the noise scale of the reference score, so this probe detects no illicit signal in this snapshot — evidence, not proof, of innocence (a nonlinear model might still exploit it); the exclusion stays, at zero cost.

objective.minimises: nothing — a control re-run of the stage-6 pipeline with one extra column
objective.reports: the balanced-accuracy change from restoring each suspect column, against the reference score's fold standard error

artifacts.description: Per suspect column: reference score, score with the column restored, delta (balanced accuracy, 5-fold host-grouped CV, identical pipeline).

checks.description: Delta vs the reference score's fold-se noise scale, per suspect column.
checks.notes: no illicit signal detected by this probe. Warn (not fail) when confirmed, because the shipped pipeline never contained the column.

caveats: Probe run on the logistic pipeline (the most attributable model, matching the reference); a tree ensemble might exploit the column differently — probe-relative conclusion only.
The with-column score is not achievable performance; it exists to justify the exclusion.

glossary.definition: TESS Object of Interest: a candidate transit signal alerted for follow-up. Several TOIs can share one host star (`tid`), which is why splits group by host.
Follow-up working group verdict per TOI: CP/KP confirmed or known planet, FP/FA false positive or alarm — the supervised classes; PC/APC are still open and excluded here.
Train/test and CV folds that move whole host stars, never cutting one across the boundary — rows sharing a star share every stellar column, so ungrouped splits leak.
Mean of per-class recalls; immune to class-balance drift, comparable across snapshots whose balance differs (this one is ~50/50, the reference was 46/54).
Score of always predicting the training majority class, computed under the same split or folds as the models it floors.
The full pipeline re-scored with labels permuted (as host-star blocks here), repeated; any real score must clear this distribution, which floors the whole pipeline rather than the labels' marginal.
Probability a random planet outranks a random false positive under the model's score; threshold-free, says nothing about calibration or any single operating point.
Whether predicted probabilities match observed frequencies; ECE is the bin-count-weighted mean gap between them.
Re-running the identical pipeline with a deliberately excluded suspect column restored; a gain beyond fold noise confirms the column carries label information it should not.
